text: The Cayley–Hamilton theorem states that every square matrix satisfies its own ___ polynomial.
explanation: p_A(λ) = det(λI − A) and p_A(A) = 0. One payoff: Aⁿ (and A⁻¹ when det A ≠ 0) can be rewritten as a polynomial in A of degree < n; note the 'proof' that substitutes A directly into det(λI − A) is a classic fallacy.
